tools.description:
Search the message history of every channel in this server (by meaning and by keywords).

Recent matches rank slightly higher unless `before`/`after` is given. Older
messages already shown to you in this conversation are not returned.
tools.name: search_messages

after.description: Only messages sent at or after this time (ISO 8601, UTC).

before.description: Only messages sent before this time (ISO 8601, UTC).

channel.description:
Only messages in this channel, like #general. Leave it out to
search the whole server.

query.description: What to look for, in natural language or keywords.

tools.description: Fetch the messages around one message in its channel, plus what it replied to.
tools.name: get_message_context

message_id.description: The `id` of a message from search results.

tools.description:
Read a channel's messages in time order, threads included: everything said
between two points, not ranked matches.

Use it to catch someone up ("what did I miss", "what happened last night",
"summarize #general today") or to follow a stretch of conversation from start to
finish. Use search_messages to find something specific, and get_message_context
for just the few messages around one hit.

With `after`, it reads forward from that point; without it, it returns the newest
messages (before `before`, if given). Long stretches come in pages: when
`cursor` is in the result, pass it back with the same other arguments for the
next page. `total_in_range` says how many messages the whole stretch has.
tools.name: channel_history

after.description:
Only messages after this point: an ISO 8601 time (UTC unless it has an
offset, like 2026-10-18T02:00-04:00) or a message ID.

before.description: Only messages before this point: a time or a message ID, as `after`.

channel.description: The channel to read, like #general. Leave it out for this channel.

limit.description: Maximum messages in this page, up to 100.

tools.description:
Count messages in this server exactly: totals and leaderboards.

Use this, not search_messages, for "who says X the most", "how often does Y
come up", "how many times", "who talks most in #channel" or trends over time:
search only returns a few examples, so counting its hits is wrong. Returns the
total and, with `group_by`, the top groups by count, each with an example
message link to cite. Counts messages (not repeats within one), excluding bots
and deleted messages.
tools.name: count_messages

after.description: Only messages sent at or after this time (ISO 8601, UTC).

before.description: Only messages sent before this time (ISO 8601, UTC).

channel.description: Only messages in this channel, like #general.

group_by.description:
"person" or "channel" for a ranking, "month" or "year" (UTC)
for counts over time. Leave it out for just the total.

limit.description: How many top groups to return, up to 50.

pattern.description:
A case-insensitive regex the text must match, for exact
spellings, short or common words, emoji or slang (`\bslay\b`).
With a query, it narrows the query's matches, which is faster.

person.description:
Only messages by this person: a ref like u2 (best), an @username,
or a name they've gone by.

query.description:
Full-text words a message must all contain, matched by stem ("slay"
also finds "slayed"). Supports "exact phrase", `or` and -word. Leave
both query and pattern out to count every message.

tools.description:
Look at the images in one message: a single image or a whole gallery.

Another model looks at them and describes each image in detail (with any
text in it), and a gallery as a whole.
tools.name: read_image

message_id.description:
The message ID shown with its images, like "[image: cat.png;
message 123]", or a message `id` from search results.

question.description:
Optional: what you want to know about them, so the
description covers it.

tools.description:
Read what you remember about a person or thing: their base profile, or one of their docs.

The result also lists all of the subject's docs (title, what belongs there, size), so
you can read a more specific one next.

doc.description: Which doc to read. Leave it out for the base profile.

subject.description:
A person's ref like u2 (best), an @username or a name they've gone by; or
the name of a thing (a pet, a place, a game, an inside joke).

tools.description: Search your memory docs about everyone and everything in this server, by keywords.
tools.name: search_memory

subject.description: Only this person or thing's docs.

tools.description:
Save one thing you learned about a person or thing, so you know it in later conversations.

One claim per call, written so it makes sense on its own ("works night shifts at the
hospital", "thinks the Eras tour was overrated"). Leave out `doc` to have it filed in
the subject's best-matching doc. The result names where it went and similar entries
already saved.

Changing a saved entry (`replaces`) needs evidence in proportion to how settled it is:
opinions change with one message; facts that have stood for months need several.
Without `sources`, the evidence is the subject's latest message in this conversation.
tools.name: remember

doc.description: A doc of the subject to put it in, from recall's list.

kind.description:
"fact" for things that are true of them (job, pets, history, relationships);
"opinion" for views, tastes and feelings, theirs or the group's about them.

replaces.description:
The ID (like e12) of an entry this corrects or updates. Same text
confirms that entry instead.

sources.description: Message IDs from search results that show it.

subject.description: A person's ref like u2 (best), an @username or a name; or a thing's name.

text.description: The claim, at most 60 words, in your own words.

tools.description:
Retire a saved entry that turned out wrong or outdated, or that someone asked you to forget.

Needs the same evidence as changing it (see remember), unless the person it's about
asked you to forget it themselves in this conversation.
tools.name: forget

sources.description: Message IDs from search results showing it's wrong or outdated.

tools.description:
Make a new doc for a subject, moving entries into it from a full or crowded one.

Each doc holds at most 1024 words; remember tells you when one is full and how to split.
tools.name: split_doc

from_doc.description: The doc to move them from.

move_entries.description: Entry IDs (like e12) to move. Empty creates an empty doc.

new_doc.description:
Short lowercase slug, like "music" or "work-history". An existing doc of
the subject also works, if it has room.

subject.description: The same subject as in remember.

summary.description: One line saying what belongs in this doc; you'll find the doc by it later.

tools.description:
Make a picture. It's drawn after your reply and posted as its own message.

Use it when someone asks for a picture, drawing, meme or visual, or when one
would clearly land better than words. Your reply goes out first and lets them
know it's on the way; the picture follows in about half a minute, replying to
their message, with your caption. If drawing fails, you get to tell them.
A picture the context lists as still being drawn is on its way: don't queue
it again unless someone asks for something different.

Name every person, pet or thing whose real look matters in `subjects`: the
drawing step finds photos of them in the server's history (and people's
avatars), checks them, and gives them to the image model as numbered
references with what to keep the same, so their likeness carries over.
tools.name: generate_image

Pictured.description: Someone or something in the picture.

description.description: Who or what they are and what they look like, as far as you know from the chat or memory, like "traumagotchi's dog, a small fluffy white mutt".

name.description: What to call them in the picture, like "Ethan" or "Nougie".

person.description: Their ref, like u2, when it's someone in this server.

photos.description: IDs of messages whose images show them, when you or the people asking already picked some (like the message in [image: …; message 123]; a Discord message or attachment link they pasted works too). Otherwise leave it empty: the drawing step finds their photos in the server's history.

Pictured.title: Pictured

aspect_ratio.description:
3:4 or 4:3 for an everyday phone photo, 9:16 or 16:9 for
tall or wide scenes, 1:1 for icons; square when left out.

caption.description: Your words to post with the picture, written for it.

edit.description:
True to change a posted photo rather than make a new picture: put
its message ID first in the first subject's photos, and the prompt
says only what to change; everything else is kept.

prompt.description:
The picture, self-contained and literal (the image model knows
nothing of the chat or the joke). Say what kind of image it is first,
then the scene: who does what, where, with framing, gaze, hands and
how they interact with things ("full body, looking down at the
needle"); then camera and light as concrete cues ("phone photo at eye
level, harsh fluorescent light") rather than mood words alone; then
constraints. Any text in it goes in quotes with where it sits and
"no other text". Call subjects by their names. Get real-world details
right (a lumbar puncture goes in the lower back between the
vertebrae). To edit, say only what changes.

style.description:
Only when they asked for one or the joke needs it, like "90s anime"
or "oil painting". Leave it out for the default: a real, candid
phone-camera photo without retouching.

subjects.description:
The people, pets and things in it whose look matters, you
included (me: true) when you're in it.
